clue.text: Pal is hot, ill — doctor may be here

indicators.note: ill suggests something out of sorts, so these letters are disordered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A friend is feverish and unwell, so naturally a doctor is to be found nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' is the anagram signal applied to PAL IS HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a building where medical staff treat patients is somewhere a doctor may be found.

clue.text: Zero quiet periods in staged entertainments

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
eras are periods of time

explanation.surface: Theatre productions with no quiet moments at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Works of musical drama are performed on a stage for entertainment.

clue.text: Disciple repentant finally, embraced by Lord

indicators.note: embraced by says that letter is hugged inside the word for a lord

parts.note: a peer is a lord

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of repentant

explanation.surface: A follower who has finally repented is welcomed into God's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon called Peter was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.

clue.text: Avert the face from performance with a team going under

indicators.note: going under, in a down clue, puts the team beneath the earlier pieces

parts.note: a turn is an act or performance on stage
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Someone looks away from a show in which a team gets beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to look away, shifting one's gaze or face aside.

clue.text: Most juicy book about powerful female — desire to get hold of it

indicators.note: to get hold of says the desire grips the book inside it

parts.note: lust is strong desire
She is H. Rider Haggard's novel about the formidable queen Ayesha

explanation.surface: A racy novel about a powerful woman inspiring lust.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush fruit or vegetation is rich and succulent; the superlative is juiciest.

clue.text: Humble way followed by saint

indicators.note: followed by says the saint's letters come after the way's in the answer

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: A modest path trodden behind a holy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone humble does not boast about themselves.

clue.text: A long way for Davis, the jazz musician

definitions.meaning: a great distance, many units of length

explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the unit of distance, and the first name of jazz trumpeter Davis.

clue.text: Head of Department is leading programme of study, giving lecture

indicators.note: Head of picks the opening letter of Department

parts.note: a course is a programme of study

explanation.surface: The head of department is running a course and giving a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a discourse is a formal spoken or written treatment of a subject.

clue.text: Experienced diner may want food thus enhanced

definitions.text: diner may want food thus enhanced
definitions.meaning: food flavoured with salt, pepper or spices

explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned campaigner is experienced; seasoned food has added salt and spices.

clue.text: Counsellor taking fellows to eminence in Devon?

parts.note: fellows are men
a tor is a rocky hill, typical of Dartmoor in the English county of Devon

explanation.surface: An adviser escorting a group of men up a hill in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England whose moors are dotted with rocky hills called tors.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a trusted adviser who guides a less experienced person.

clue.text: Representative of death in play?

parts.note: a sales representative, as in Arthur Miller's play Death of a ...

explanation.surface: Someone portraying Death on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an actor playing the Grim Reaper; in fact it points to the travelling rep of Arthur Miller's play title.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales representative or rep is a commercial traveller, the subject of Miller's famous tragedy.

clue.text: Vehicle taking hundred to match, first to leave

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: first to leave tells us the opening letter of the word for match is dropped

parts.note: a match can be a marriage, as in a good match

explanation.surface: A car taking a hundred guests to a wedding, with the first ones departing.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-drawn coach or railway coach is a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Pimple at side of leg? You've got it!

indicators.note: at side of places the cricket term next to the pimple, after it

parts.note: a spot is a pimple
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so leg gives ON

explanation.surface: A doctor finds a blemish on the side of a patient's leg and declares the diagnosis correct.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the half of the field behind a right-handed batsman's legs is the leg side or on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an exclamation that something is exactly right, as when a guess hits the mark.

clue.text: Procedural matter that is troubling to poor friend

indicators.note: troubling suggests disturbance, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Bureaucratic red tape is causing grief to a hard-up pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubling' is the anagram signal for TO POOR FRIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: In a meeting, a query about whether the rules of debate are being followed is a procedural issue.

clue.text: Power coming to pulpit activity

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
coming to a place is reaching it

explanation.surface: Strength arriving at the pulpit.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivering sermons is what a minister does from the pulpit.

clue.text: Female over coffee looking embarrassed to be buttered up

parts.note: a latte is milky coffee
embarrassed people go red

explanation.surface: A woman over a coffee blushes after being showered with compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to butter someone up is to praise them insincerely to win favour.

clue.text: Voluntary work gets a lot in after training

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: after training suggests being drilled into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Voluntary work earns plenty, once you've been trained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after training' rearranges A LOT IN into TIONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something optional is left to choice rather than compulsory.

clue.text: Component of birthday tea? That's very easy!

definitions.meaning: a single slice of the cake served at a birthday party
an idiom for a task requiring no effort

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a slice of the birthday cake; idiomatically, something extremely simple to do.

clue.text: Shows hesitation, fine changes being needed

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
alters means changes

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates because a fine needs some adjustments.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to waver or stumble, losing confidence or momentum.

clue.text: One who may be looking for a permanent job involving some winter nights

definitions.text: One who may be looking for a permanent job

indicators.note: involving some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A worker on a temporary placement who must put in some winter nights.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'involving' in the definition; it belongs with 'some' as the hidden-word signal, and the definition ends at 'job'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee on a temporary placement often hopes it leads to a permanent post.

clue.text: Olympic event brings endless debate

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the word for debate is cut off

parts.note: to debate a matter is to discuss it

explanation.surface: An Olympic competition sparks interminable argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the heavy disc is a field event at the Olympic Games.

clue.text: Good-looking products finally taken to market

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of products

parts.note: a mart is a market

explanation.surface: Attractive goods are at last brought to market.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: smart means stylish and well turned out.

clue.text: Much less solitary with others being brought in

indicators.note: being brought in says the word for others goes inside the word for solitary

parts.note: solitary means lone
et al, Latin et alii, means and others

explanation.surface: Someone is far less lonely now that other people have been invited along.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom used after a negative: 'cannot walk, much less run' equals 'cannot walk, never mind run'.

clue.text: See copper, male who may be standing in for colleague?

definitions.text: who may be standing in for colleague?

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Spot the policeman, a man who might be covering for a fellow officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who temporarily stands in for another.

clue.text: Private home, the thing gone round by friend

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: gone round says the little word for the thing is turned backwards

parts.note: the thing is it
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A personal residence whose object of attention has been circled by a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: intimate details are personal and confidential, not public.

clue.text: Saturn maybe in lecture

definitions.meaning: the Saturn V was the launch vehicle of the Apollo missions, an example of the answer

explanation.surface: A talk about the planet Saturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saturn' looks like the planet, but it is the Apollo launcher; the second sense is British informal for a reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saturn V was a space launcher; 'a rocket' is also British slang for a severe reprimand.

clue.text: Bishop has amusing setback

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
light entertainment is amusing

explanation.surface: A cleric suffers a comic misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A blight is a spoiling influence or misfortune that holds something back.

clue.text: Waters flowing back — chaps collected sludge

indicators.note: collected says the reversed waters take the chaps inside them
flowing back says the word for waters is read in reverse

parts.note: tides are moving waters of the sea
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Ebbing water leaves behind men and muck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing back' gives SEDIT; 'Waters' looks like the definition, but the definition is 'sludge' at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid forms a muddy deposit.
